newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Cr.Lyonnais Portugal unit sells retail network.
newsitem.headline: Cr.Lyonnais Portugal unit sells retail network.

text.p: Credit Lyonnais Portugal (CLP), the local unit of French state controlled bank Credit Lyonnais, has agreed to sell its retail network to Spanish bank Caixa da Galicia, CLP said on Friday.
A statement said CLP would continue its activities in the large companies and capital market in Portugal.
"Credit Lyonnais Portugal has agreed in principle with Caixa da Galicia to sell to the Spanish group its retail activities in Portugal," it said.

The sale includes 21 branches, its private banking, marketing and communication divisions, its telephone banking unit Telecredit and its investment fund unit, Sociedade Gestora de Fundos de Investimento Mobiliario (SGFIM), it added.

"Credit Lyonnais Portugal will remain in the market for large companies and in the capital market, aiming to continue its involvement in these areas in line with a strategy set by the Credit Lyonnais group for Europe," the statement said.
The value of the deal, which is subject to the approval of regulatory authorities, was not disclosed.
Earlier, Portugal's Financial Markets Committee (CMVM) suspended trade in CLP.

A new recovery plan for the French bank Credit Lyonnais, recently submitted to the European Commission, focuses on improving the profitability of the group and the disposal of Lyonnais' retail banking network outside France.
CLP, which employs 330 people, posted a net profit of 362 million escudos ($1.92 million) in 1996.
Caixa da Galicia registered a 1996 net profit of more than 25.5 billion escudos. It has 500 branches in Spain and seven abroad, and employs 3,096 people. ($1=188.878 escudos)
